label: NOTE: what this set reaches, and the three checks that exist only to reach it
why: V92Modulator's constructor and destructor and t_v92mod.cpp were written by one hand at one sitting from one reading of .text+0x14050-0x153fb and of the standalone `reset` at +0x15060. Every entry below is a claim the disassembly makes: the five-sixths rounding, which of the five raw buffers is sized from the ARGUMENT and which from the derived block, the six sub-object sizes and their constructor arguments, the seven argument stores, the inlined `reset`'s nine writes and its priming loop, and eleven null tests. THREE OF THE CLAIMS ARE BEHIND POISONED POINTERS AND HAVE A CHECK OF THEIR OWN: the scrambler's near tap (compared as a DISTANCE between its pointers), the priming loop's trip count (read off the queue's write cursor), and every allocation size (compared as `harness_alloc.bytes` against the reference, which is the ONLY witness the five raw buffers have). WHAT NO ENTRY HERE CAN REACH: the resampler being released through its vtable rather than by an explicit destructor call and a free -- the two spellings free the same memory in the same order, and the difference is an instruction sequence, not a behaviour (finding F1286). Nor the order of the eleven releases, nor the sixteen members this batch does not write.

why: PROVABLY unobservable THROUGH THE CONSTRUCTOR, WHICH IS ALL THIS SUITE DRIVES. `Scrambler<T,I>::Scrambler` ends in `reset(0)` -- see include/dsplib/Scrambler.h -- and `reset` writes only the three cursors, from `pInitOut`, `pInitTap1` and `pInitTap2`, and the history between them; none of those inputs changes between the member-initialiser and the end of the constructor body, so the second call stores exactly what the first did. Dropping it is the identity there. THE FIND-STRING NOW LIVES IN `V92Modulator::reset` ITSELF, because that member is written and the constructor calls it rather than a file-static copy of its body (finding F5902) -- and it is NOT the identity in that member, which runs over a scrambler that has been processing. The marker stays correct for THIS suite because t_v92mod.cpp reaches the statement only through the constructor and never calls `reset` on a used object. The catchable version this `why` used to predict now exists: `test/mutations/v92modstate.json`, "reset does not put the scrambler back", against t_v92modstate.cpp, which dirties the scrambler first. The idempotence is read out of Scrambler's source, not inferred from a green run.

label: the phase 3 modulator's null test is dropped
the bit-to-symbol stage's null test is dropped
the resampler's null test is dropped
why: PROVABLY unobservable, and by the language rather than by the optimiser. `delete p` over a null `p` is required to do nothing, so GCC emits its own `test`/`je` around the vtable call whatever we write; the explicit `if` in front of it folds into that one test, which is why the blob has exactly ONE `test %edx,%edx` here and not two. Removing ours therefore leaves the guard in place. It is kept in the source because it is the shape the other ten releases have and because the fixture drives this pointer null in 1,024 of its 2,048 subsets -- but the entry has to be marked rather than removed, so that nobody later reads a green run as evidence the spelling was tested. Verified by compiling both forms and comparing the text, not by reasoning alone.
